newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Crude Outlook - Refinery outages key for Minas.
newsitem.headline: Asia Crude Outlook - Refinery outages key for Minas.

text.p: Asian crude sales for prompt trading are expected to slow this week as Middle East grades appear mostly placed, while Indonesian refineries are the focus for Minas and Duri sellers.

The unexpected and prolonged shutdown of the 125,000 barrel- per-day (bpd) crude distillation unit (CDU) at the Balongan refinery and the scheduled shutdown of the 120,000-bpd Dumai refinery for maintenance has led to an overhang of Minas and Duri.
March prices of both plummeted to ICP less 50/60 cents per barrel in recent weeks, but appear steadier now as initial export allocations from Pertamina have been placed.
But traders said two million barrels of Duri have been put into floating storage, leaving players worried on whether the crude is to be released onto the spot market.
The Duri was floating off the Dumai refinery last week and made room for Minas to be put into storage at the refinery. Minas represents 70 percent of Dumai's feedstock and Duri 30 percent.
"If it's dumped you could see a $1.00 discount," one trader said.
But another trader said the Duri was being held pending the start up of the two refineries. Balongan uses mostly Duri for its crude runs.
That left the key question of when Balongan would restart its CDU.
The CDU has failed attempts to restart amid technical problems at an 83,000-bpd residue catalytic cracker at Balongan.
"It could come back up any minute. Pertamina needs to provide sufficient Duri for it to run," one affiliate said.
Traders said if the CDU comes back up it would provide great relief to the beleagured Minas and Duri market.
In February, benchmark Minas traded as high as $1.45 above its official selling price. In March, with the two refineries down, prices swung into a deep discount.
Interest to buy Duri from blenders and some traders checking the arbitrage potential into the United States helped price talk rise to ICP -30/-20 and even to flat.
But others said while two million barrels of Duri were in floating storage, it would weigh on the price. Some traders said Duri should be valued more in a range of ICP -50/-20.
Middle East grades were now largely looking towards April trading.
Traders said they expected a stronger premium month for May trading also.

Most grades fell into discount for April trading because of relatively strong January OSPs versus published Dubai levels. But the February OSPs were cut, helping relieve some of the downward pressure on differentials.
In addition, most Japanese and South Korean maintenance turnarounds are in May, said one trader. So any buying for May liftings will be for June arrivals.
"I expect next month to be stronger," he said. "The highest turnarounds are in May."
--Singapore Newsroom (+65 870 3081)
